outputs: advice in natural language to help individuals facing real-world situations

changes_made.explanation: Normalized model names to standard forms (GPT-3 instead of GPT3), removed duplicates and simplified output descriptions
Paper explicitly states they use human evaluation rather than automatic metrics
No LLMs were used as judges/evaluators in this paper

guideline: Workers are given a situation and two pieces of advice (one human-written, one model-generated)
Workers choose which advice is more helpful (Definitely A/B, Slightly A/B)
Workers rate the worse advice on helpfulness scale (Slightly helpful, Not helpful, Dangerous)
Workers answer diagnostic questions about meaning vs writing problems and applicability to other situations

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated and normalized criteria descriptions, removed redundant entries

overall_notes: The paper focuses on generative NLG evaluation through the TuringAdvice task. It uses Mechanical Turk workers for human evaluation with a detailed pairwise comparison protocol. No automatic metrics are used. The extraction was generally accurate but needed normalization of model names and consolidation of evaluation criteria.
